author: Maryland State Wire
title: Washington College renews partnership with Kent and Queen Anne's County schools
text:
Washington College renews partnership with Kent and Queen Anne’s County schools
Washington College signed a memorandum of understanding with Kent County and Queen Anne’s County school districts to continue building opportunities for current teachers, teachers in training, and public school students, according to an Aug. 19 announcement.
Education professor Sara Clarke-De Reza led the process to create the new agreement, which seeks to deepen teacher education and dual enrollment programs while expanding collaboration, particularly around civic engagement. Clarke-De Reza said, "While the Education Department has long tended our public school relationships, it's time for Washington College to take on, at an institutional level, the stewardship of these mission-critical partnerships. This new agreement formally acknowledges the many ways our institutions support and strengthen one another and provides an opportunity to bring new energy to our future work."
Since 1978, Washington College education students have completed teaching internships at both county public schools. High school students from both systems have also participated in dual enrollment classes and summer internships at the college in recent years. The renewed memorandum of understanding aims not only to reinforce these existing initiatives but also to introduce additional opportunities for student engagement.
Kent County Public Schools Superintendent Mary McComas said about the partnership, "It was time for a renaissance. What I really find exciting about the partnership is the dual enrollment aspect, expanding local students’ opportunities to take courses near their home on a college campus." Queen Anne’s County Public Schools Superintendent Matt Kibler identified dual enrollment as one of the most exciting aspects of the agreement and highlighted its value for first-generation college students.
This fall, Washington College will welcome 16 high school seniors from Kent and Queen Anne’s counties for dual enrollment classes—a continuation of several years of double-digit participation in a program that had only attracted a handful of students as recently as 2022.
President Bryan Matthews said before signing, "This kind of a partnership is just critical. It is so important because of the impact we have on each other. It is just a really exciting way to not just talk about it, but after a lot of hard work, have a real partnership taking existing programs to the next level."
